static_traits.name: Chen Shan
static_traits.social_status: A few friends to confide in, but not yet fully sharing his negative-thinking troubles with them; tense relationships with colleagues due to his negative reactions to mistakes.
static_traits.medical_history: Never experienced similar psychological problems; never received psychotherapy or counseling; no major physical illness.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, can describe events and emotions concretely; willing to cooperate and try exercises; slightly negative but open attitude; anxiety present with tension, prone to rumination and self-reproach.

basic_info.main_problem: I tend to catastrophize small mistakes, leading to intense suffering and negative emotions.
basic_info.core_demands: After realizing that the negative thinking pattern is affecting my work performance and overall happiness, I decided to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: About a year ago he messed up a customer's order at work; though he apologized on the spot and fixed it immediately, he kept ruminating that day and strongly worried about being complained about or blamed by the boss, first experiencing high-intensity stress and fear of unemployment; since then similar negative thinking has been triggered almost daily in the cafe's high-pressure situations.

Once spilled coffee at work, thinking he would be blamed or mocked continuously, but others just reacted calmly and it quickly passed; though the outcome was not serious, he still worried at the time about 'being talked about forever'.

core_beliefs: I am not competent in my work

special_situations.event: Gets a customer's order wrong while working at a cafe
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I make a mistake, it means I am incompetent and may be blamed or even lose my job.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately apologizes and corrects the order; afterward tries to soothe herself with rationality and emphasizing positives, but still repeatedly thinks about the mistake.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The whole day is ruined; the boss will be angry; I might be fired.

special_situations.event: After the mistake the boss did not clearly respond or stayed silent, and he speculated about the other's attitude
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others do not immediately give positive feedback, they are often dissatisfied or angry.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces interaction with colleagues and falls into self-blame and worry to avoid being evaluated.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: The boss is angry with me; colleagues will look down on me.

special_situations.event: During high-pressure periods, makes minor mistakes (such as flustered hands, small process errors)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Any mistake proves I am not good enough, not suited for this job.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Demanding perfection of himself, excessive self-monitoring; ruminating continuously once a mistake happens.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This proves I am not competent in this job.

special_situations.event: After spilling coffee, worried about being continuously blamed, but others actually handled it indifferently and it soon passed
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once a mistake is made, he will keep being blamed afterward and the event will keep affecting him.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: After the event, repeatedly recalls details, magnifies negative consequences, and finds it hard to attend to the actually stable outcome.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will keep being talked about for this matter; the consequences will stay very bad.

core_conflict.wish: Desiring to be recognized and accepted at work, seen as competent and safe
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated, blamed, or fired, losing stability and self-worth
defense_goal: Avoiding criticism and punishment by maintaining high standards and self-vigilance, in order to maintain a sense of safety

object_relations.self_representation: An employee prone to mistakes who may be negated
object_relations.object_representation: Authority figures / colleagues potentially dissatisfied, who may criticize or punish him

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the other has not yet given clear positive feedback after a mistake, or stays silent
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting his own anxiety as others' dissatisfaction or anger, believing the boss or colleagues are blaming him (transference: projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a supportive, empathic tone, gently clarifying the gap between assumptions and facts, inviting him to examine evidence and return to present experience; avoiding evaluative and confrontational language, using open-ended questioning to help him distinguish others' attitudes from his own feelings.

manifestations: Living alone; tense relationships with colleagues; having friends but not yet fully sharing his troubles, limited emotional support

contact_model.definition: The individual has poor self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism and rumination after mistakes
Self-limiting from fear of being unable to do well
Hard to directly express real troubles to friends and colleagues

exception_events.target_problem: When making a small mistake at work, the client usually engages in catastrophic thinking, persistent rumination, and strong worry about being blamed by the boss or fired.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once after messing up a customer's order, the client apologized on the spot and fixed it immediately; the customer accepted and left calmly, and the boss never raised criticism afterwards, the actual consequences being mild.
exception_events.reason: Different approach: apologizing and fixing immediately; different situation / support: the customer was calm, the boss did not blame, so the anticipated severe consequences never appeared.

exception_events.target_problem: When a sudden small mistake happens (like spilling coffee), the client usually anticipates long-term blame and sinks into rumination and negative emotions.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In one coffee-spilling incident, colleagues and others just handled it calmly and it quickly passed, with no lasting blame or negative follow-up.
exception_events.reason: Different situation: others reacted calmly and tolerantly, the incident was resolved quickly, reducing prolonged negative feedback.

positive_force: When mistakes occur, has the ability to correct promptly and apologize
Willing to seek counseling and try self-compassion and cognitive restructuring exercises
Able to identify his own catastrophizing pattern and admit possible overreaction
Has some social support (several friends to talk with)
negative_force: Tendency toward catastrophizing, black-and-white, mental filtering, and negating-the-positive thinking
Excessively worries about others' evaluations and job security, tending toward mind reading and negative predictions
Rumination and self-reproach maintaining anxiety and low mood
High-pressure work situations frequently triggering negative cognitions and bodily tension responses

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophizing and strong anxiety after small mistakes, persistent rumination and self-reproach
antecedent: Minor mistakes occur (such as order errors, spilling coffee)
Worrying about customer complaints or the boss's dissatisfaction
target_behavior.core_reason: High worry about losing work and being blamed / negated, interpreting small mistakes as signs of serious consequences (catastrophic thinking).
target_behavior.function: Escaping the threat of being criticized or fired (trying self-protection through hypervigilance and self-criticism).
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance affected; tense relationships with colleagues; overall mood and decreased motivation; troubled by negative thinking almost daily.
